title: Naval on saving yourself: long-term selfish virtue, explore-then-invest, and choosing your environment
summary: Naval and Eric Jorgenson revisit Almanac ideas. Virtues are long-term selfishness, and a mission bigger than yourself pulls people in. Authenticity means dropping the mask. Life runs on exploring widely, then investing for compound returns. Judgment comes from deliberate iterations, not hours. Choose your environment and take inspiration over envy.

principles.text: Virtues are long-term selfishness; the modern devil is cheap dopamine that feels good now and hurts later.
principles.quote: all the virtues if you were to follow them as an individual on a long enough time frame, they would make you individually better off.

principles.text: A mission larger than yourself becomes a rallying point that assembles talented people around you.
principles.quote: by having that mission be larger than about yourself you assemble people.

principles.text: Authenticity is not wearing a mask; drop the persona and the wrong people and situations fall away.
principles.quote: I view authenticity as an output of not pretending to be someone or something other than you are.

principles.text: Explore widely until you find fit, then invest, because compound interest drives all the benefits in life.
principles.quote: you should explore widely until you find a fit. But then all the benefits in life come from compound interest.

principles.text: Learning comes from deliberate iterations: act, honestly reflect, change, retry. Not hours or repetitions.
principles.quote: Iteration means you do something, then you honestly reflect upon the outcome, you make a change and you try again.

principles.text: Intelligence is choosing the right things to want, then getting them. Choose your environment consciously.
principles.quote: the only true test of intelligence is if you get what you want out of life, right? And I, that one's one of my favorites for myself because it's a two-part test.
